title: Tenant-aware analytics replication orchestration and residency enforcement
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Problem: The Console backend currently writes aggregated usage metrics and event streams to a single global analytics pipeline which then persists to a primary region. Customers with data residency requirements and tenants in EU/APAC need guarantees that identifiable telemetry and derived analytics either remain in-region or are restricted per legal tags.

Goal: Implement tenant-aware replication orchestration that routes, transforms, and stores analytics streams according to tenant residency policies. This includes tagging events with residency metadata, enforcing legal_tag constraints at ingestion, selective cross-region replication, per-region storage targets (S3/GCS buckets), KMS key selection, and audit logs for compliance. The system should minimize cost and latency impact for global tenants while ensuring strong guarantees for regulated tenants.

Scope: backend services responsible for analytics ingestion and replication (changefeeds / CDC -> transform layer -> region sinks), metadata service for tenant residency and legal tags, orchestration policy engine, and console controls for SRE/PM to set residency policies and view replication state. Does not include analytics query layer changes (tracked in ENG-20399).

acceptance_criteria: All ingestion events for tenants with residency_policy=IN_REGION are stored only in the tenant's designated region bucket and are not replicated out-of-region.
Legal_tagged events are blocked or redacted before any cross-region publish when policy disallows replication.
Metadata service can be queried via Console API and visible in the Console UI for operators and admins.
End-to-end tests that simulate regional failover preserve residency guarantees and produce audit logs for each replicated event.
Performance: 95th percentile additional ingestion latency due to routing < 20ms for non-regulated tenants; <50ms budget for regulated tenants under typical load.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable tenant-aware routing for 5 pilot tenants in eu-west-1, no UI exposure; monitor metrics and audit logs.
Phase 2 (opt-in): expose Console toggles for selected customers, run canary for 2 weeks with tighter SLOs.
Phase 3 (enforced): migrate existing regulated tenants to enforced residency_policy with migration jobs and a 30-day audit window.
Rollback: fallback to global pipeline with a compensating audit marker and safe-delete window for cross-region copies.
risks_mitigations: Risk: Increased operational cost from multiple regional sinks. Mitigation: implement tiered retention for cross-region artifacts and memoize prefix/KV caching to reduce duplicate processing.
Risk: Incorrect tenant tagging at source. Mitigation: add schema validation and a staging-validator that rejects untagged messages, with visibility in the Console.
Risk: KMS key misconfiguration leading to unreadable artifacts. Mitigation: automated pre-deploy KMS mapping checks and emergency key-rotation runbooks.
testing_plan: Unit tests for policy engine (residency_policy and legal_tag rules).
Integration tests that deploy consumer/transform pods in multiple regions using localstack/GCP emulator for buckets.
Chaos tests: simulate region failover and network partitions; assert no out-of-region writes for IN_REGION tenants.
Load test: replicate peak traffic patterns from prod (sampled) and measure replication lag and cost delta.
notes: Consider leveraging existing routing work from ENG-1845 (model routing) for policy engine primitives.
We should add a lightweight GDPR-friendly pseudonymization pass for EU regulated tenants before any non-authorized processing.
